tagline: Down US 93 past a gunfight town and spires of clay.
intro: From US 6 and 50 at Majors Place the byway follows US 93 south for nearly 150 miles, down to Pioche, through the Meadow Valley past Panaca and Caliente, and west to the junction near Crystal Springs where State Routes 318 and 375 come in. The road was once part of State Route 7, which ran nearly 250 miles from Ely through Pioche and Caliente to Crystal Springs and beyond.
Panaca, a mile off the highway, was founded as a Mormon colony in 1864 and is the only community in Nevada that forbids the sale of alcohol.

moments.title: Pioche
moments.text: Local lore has 72 men killed in gunfights in this silver camp before its first natural death, a legend kept on at Boot Hill.

moments.title: Cathedral Gorge State Park
moments.text: Two miles northwest of Panaca, erosion has carved soft bentonite clay into spires and cave-like forms, the backdrop in the 1920s for open-air plays and Easter ceremonies.

moments.title: Caliente
moments.text: Named for its hot springs, Caliente grew past 5,000 people as a railroad town and shrank with the coming of diesel, and its 1923 mission-style depot still stands.
